title: Quantization profiles: best practices and rollout playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's recommended quantization profiles, evaluation criteria, and an operational rollout playbook. It is intended for model owners, inference engineers, and applied ML teams responsible for onboarding models into the serving runtime. The goal is to reduce per-token cost and memory footprint while protecting output quality and reducing regression risk.

Scope

- Applies to model variants being prepared for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers INT8, mixed-precision, and simulated quantization evaluation prior to productionization.
- References the eval harness and regression triage playbooks for test suites and incident handling.

Goals

1. Standardize a small set of quantization profiles that balance cost, latency, and quality.
2. Provide deterministic evaluation steps and pass/fail criteria to avoid silent regressions.
3. Integrate quantization checks into model onboarding and CI for rollout gating.

Definitions

- Quantization profile: a named set of quantization parameters (bit width, group size, per-channel/per-tensor, kernel selection flags) applied during model export or at runtime.
- Quality delta: relative degradation in evaluation metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1, BLEU or human judgement score) compared to a float32 baseline.

Recommended profiles

We maintain three canonical profiles that should cover the majority of workloads. Teams may propose additional profiles only after approval from Applied ML.

| Profile name | Description | Typical savings | Recommended use cases |
|--------------|-------------|-----------------|-----------------------|
| safe-compat-8 | Per-channel INT8 with calibrated scales, group size = 1, bias correction | ~1.3-2x memory reduction, modest latency wins | High-quality chat/assistant models, core customer-facing endpoints |
| perf-8-mixed | Mixed INT8 for attention + FP16 for FFN, per-tensor quantization for less-sensitive layers | ~2-3x memory reduction, best throughput for batch workloads | Throughput-first inference, batch embeddings, non-critical generation |
| low-bit-rand | Experimental Q4-bit or 4-bit group quantization with activation remapping | ~3-4x memory reduction, higher risk of quality loss | Internal cost experiments, closed beta, not recommended for public endpoints |

Evaluation checklist (pre-merge CI and pre-production validation)

1. Unit tests: quantized kernels pass numeric smoke tests (max abs diff, relative error within thresholds).
2. Eval harness: run the model's canonical prompt set (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks guidelines) under the quantized profile and float32 baseline. Collect metrics: perplexity, task-specific metrics, and 200 seeded deterministic prompts for regression checks.
3. Human-in-the-loop (HITL): for generation models serving customer data, run a blind A/B quality study with at least N=100 prompts covering edge cases.
4. Latency and memory: measure p99 latency and peak GPU memory under production-like batching and sequence length distributions.

Pass/fail criteria

- Quality delta: no >2% relative degradation in core metric (or absolute degradation if metric is bounded) for safe-compat-8. For perf-8-mixed, allow up to 4% degradation with product owner sign-off. Low-bit-rand requires explicit approval and documented mitigations.
- P99 latency increase must be <= 10% for per-request SLOs; throughput must improve >= 10% for throughput targets.
- Peak GPU memory must be reduced by at least 20% compared to float32 baseline for profile to be considered beneficial.

Quantization config examples

YAML example for model export (safe-compat-8):

quantization_profile: safe-compat-8
parameters:
  weight_precision: int8
  activation_precision: fp16
  per_channel: true
  group_size: 1
  calibration_method: percentile-99.9
  bias_correction: true
  fallback_layers: ["lm_head"]

Operational rollout playbook

1. Prepare branch and CI:
   - Add quantization profile to model export configs.
   - Add eval-harness jobs: unit smoke tests, full eval suite, memory/latency benchmark.
   - Ensure model cards and release notes list the profiles tested.

2. Canary deployment (staged):
   - Canary size: 1-5% of traffic or fixed 10 concurrent sessions for low-traffic endpoints.
   - Run continuous regression checks for 48 hours. Monitor: request success rate, quality metrics from sampled prompts, latency p95/p99, and token-level cost.
   - If any regression alarm fires (see regression triage thresholds below), immediately rollback to float32 or safe-compat-8 as appropriate.

3. Broad rollout:
   - If canary stable for 72 hours with no regression and metrics within pass criteria, increase to 25% for 24 hours, then 50% for 24 hours, then full traffic. Use automatic ramp only if no alerts triggered.

4. Post-rollout validation:
   - Run a comprehensive eval-harness sweep using latest prompt sets and collect HITL feedback if applicable.
   - Update model card with observed metrics, cost savings, and known failure modes.

Regression triage thresholds (short list)

- Quality alerts:
  - Core-metric delta > passed threshold (see pass/fail criteria).
  - Human-reported severe hallucination or safety regression > 2 reports within 24 hours.
- Performance alerts:
  - P99 latency increase > 20% or absolute > SLO + 100 ms.
  - Request success rate drop > 1% absolute.

If a regression alert occurs:

1. Open a regression ticket in the applied-ml-and-evals board and tag the model owner and runtime-oncall.
2. Snapshot canary logs and sample inputs/outputs.
3. Rollback immediately if customer-facing user impact is confirmed.
4. Run regression triage playbook: reproduce locally with saved seed prompts, ablate profile settings (group size, per_channel flag, fallback layers), and re-run eval-harness.

Ownership and responsibilities

- Model owner: responsible for adding profiles to CI, reviewing HITL results, and approving broad rollouts.
- Applied ML team: provides canonical prompt sets, runs A/B studies, and adjudicates ambiguous regressions.
- Serving runtime: ensures kernel support for selected profile and provides observability hooks (token-level tracing, memory breakdowns).
- SRE: creates canary routing, monitors infra metrics and enforces SLOs.

Templates and artifacts to attach

- Quantization profile YAML template (copy into model repo).
- Eval-harness job definition (Jenkins/Github Actions snippet).
- Sample human evaluation rubric and consent templates.

References and related docs

- Applied ML eval harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Prompt sets and benchmarks guidelines: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-regression-triage-playbook-2026

Appendix: example regression triage checklist

1. Confirm reproducibility with eval-harness deterministic seed run.
2. Compare token-level log probabilities between float32 and quantized runs for failing prompts.
3. Inspect activations for layer-wise saturation or clipping.
4. Try fallback: enable per-layer FP16 for top-k deviating layers and re-evaluate.
5. If unresolved, escalate to research/applied-ml for kernel or algorithmic mitigations.
